text:
alex: Anyone else seeing ECR image pulls failing from the us-west-2 edge cluster after the NAT failover this morning? pods stuck in ImagePullBackOff.
marta: yes seeing it on cluster-edge-3, started ~08:15 UTC. curl to ECR private endpoint times out.
isha: logs show DNS resolving to VPC endpoint IPs but tcp connect fails. `dig +short 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com` returns 10.10.45.23 (vpce eni).
raj: interesting — we had a NAT gw health fail and an AZ failover, ENIs for the interface endpoint got reattached to different subnets. Could be SG or route table mismatch.
nicole: can someone run `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d --query "VpcEndpoints[?ServiceName=='com.amazonaws.us-west-2.ecr.api']"` and paste the SubnetIds + SecurityGroupIds?
alex: output: SubnetIds: [subnet-12a, subnet-34b], Groups: [sg-aaaa, sg-bbbb], PrivateDnsEnabled: true, State: available.
marta: on the host that fails `ss -tnlp | grep 443` shows no connection to 10.10.45.23:443, `tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.10.45.23` shows SYN but no SYN-ACK.
isha: that smells like SG or NACL dropping. Check source/dest on the endpoint ENI: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values:vpce --query 'NetworkInterfaces[?SubnetId==`subnet-34b`]'` then check Groups.
raj: looked into the ENI: it landed in subnet-34b but route table for that subnet points to a blackhole route (we had a transient route update during the failover). Route table main -> local, but an override to 0.0.0.0/0 pointed to a stale nat-<id> which is in deleting state.
nicole: aha. If the ENI's subnet cannot reach the NAT, the endpoint cannot complete TLS handshake to ECR (endpoint is an ENI in the VPC — egress from pods to the endpoint should be L2 within VPC, but the endpoint's replies might need egress if endpoint tries to reach service outside? Also if route propagation messed with return path it could drop).
sre-bot: Incident detected: VPC route table changed (rta-rt-67) 08:13 UTC -> propagated change: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-07de (deleting). Alerting infra-oncall.
alex: quick repro: on a node: `curl --resolve "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com:443:10.10.45.23" https://123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/v2/` -> hangs.
marta: did `traceroute -n 10.10.45.23` — only 1 hop (local), so traffic hits the ENI but no response. Could be SG inbound on the endpoint only allows the endpoint's expected security group references and our node IPs didn't get allowed after AZ migration.
isha: check the endpoint SG: `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-aaaa` shows inbound allows 10.0.0.0/8 on 443. Node IPs are 10.20.x.x (different VPC overlay for pods). Looks like we used a prefix-list previously but migration removed it.
raj: root cause hypothesis: during NAT failover we automated a route table swap and a config drift removed the prefix-list rule in the endpoint SG. When the ENI re-anchored in a different subnet, the endpoint SG no longer allowed pod CIDR, so connections got dropped (SYN in, no SYN-ACK).
nicole: mitigation: add pod CIDR ranges back into the endpoint SG, or re-enable the managed prefix-list. For immediate fix: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-aaaa --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.20.0.0/16` (one-off).
alex: applied the SG rule, pods started pulling images again within ~30s :thumbsup:.
marta: long-term we should: 1) make endpoint SG reference a prefix-list (managed) so it doesn't drift, 2) add an automation check that validates endpoint ENIs' subnets match route table state and SG rules include current pod CIDRs, 3) check Route53 resolver rules for split-horizon behavior after failover.
isha: also found a secondary problem: Route53 private hosted zone for `dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com` had an old A record mapping to the previous VPCE IPs for cross-account route. Not the main cause here but would cause cached negative results on clients with long TTL. Need to ensure VPCE private DNS is authoritative and TZ records are cleaned.
raj: agree. Action items: (1) insta-fix SG rule (done), (2) revert the blackhole route and ensure route tables point to available NAT or IGW where intended — ops oncall to confirm, (3) add a drift-detection job to eng-infra repo (PR assigned to @marta), (4) update runbook to include `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc> --query 'NetworkInterfaces[?Description==\`AWS Endpoint\`]'` step.
nicole: tagging follow-ups in pager duty ticket PD-4832.
alex: side note — adding health-checks to VPCE ENIs isn't straightforward, but we could add a simple synthetic probe from an isolated subnet to hit each endpoint IP and alert on no SYN-ACK.
marta: yep — will prototype a lambda + cloudwatch alarm.
isha: final: we should also consider enabling interface endpoint health checks in console if available, and add a kube-level fallback to public ECR via signed creds (with strict IAM) for extreme cases.
raj: closing for now, monitor for 1hr. If we see recurrence we'll open a dedicated incident.
*sre-bot pinned message*: "Runbook updated: VPCE SG drift check added to infra-monitoring repo (link)"
